*   **Plot:** The novel intertwines three seemingly separate cases:
    *   The 30-year-old disappearance of two young girls (Nina and Julia Ragg).
    *   The recent murder of a wealthy man's wife (Laura Cubitt).
    *   The search for a missing sister (Theo's sister).

*   **Series:** It spawned several sequels:

    *   *When Will There Be Good News?* (2008)
    *   *Started Early, Took My Dog* (2010)
    *   *Big Sky* (2019)
    *   *Seven Stones to Stand or Fall* (2022 - includes short stories & a novella)

*   ***Case Histories* (Compilation Album - 2010):**
    *   **Released by:** LTM Recordings (LTMCD 2550), a label specializing in reissuing post-punk and alternative music.
    *   **What it is:** A **compilation album**, **NOT** an original studio album by The Sound. It collects rare and unreleased material:
        *   Early demos (1979-1980) from *before* their debut album *Jeopardy*.
        *   BBC Radio 1 sessions (John Peel & David Jensen sessions from 1980-1982).
        *   Some live tracks.
    *   **Why the title?** The title *Case Histories* is likely a play on the band's name ("The Sound") and refers to these tracks being "case files" or historical documents of the band's development – a deep-cut reference for fans, not a mainstream title.
    *   **Obscurity:** This compilation is only known to serious post-punk collectors and fans of The Sound. It has no mainstream recognition. You won't find it on major streaming service front pages, and casual music fans have never heard of it.
    *   **Streaming Note:** Tracks from this comp might appear on The Sound's discography on Spotify/Apple Music under compilations or "Singles & EPs," but the *album* itself titled *Case Histories* is not prominent.

4.  **The Obscure Album Exists:** The technical existence of The Sound's comp validates the search for some people, even though it's irrelevant to the famous reference.
